problem: Existing navigation instruction generators (speaker models) are end-to-end networks tightly coupled to specific datasets (e.g. R2R panoramas). They give little control, produce short repetitive instructions that omit landmarks, and cannot use LLMs or transfer to new domains. Evaluation also relies on expert references or downstream agent performance.
motivation: Expert instructions are scarce and expensive, and VLN needs large-scale, high-quality instruction data. A generator that works on any egocentric trajectory, plus an evaluation that needs no human annotations, would make instruction data scalable. Instructions are built from actions, scenes and objects, so explicitly extracting these entities and recomposing them with an LLM should improve accuracy and richness.
key_idea: Decompose an egocentric navigation video into action, scene and object entities using pluggable modules, then recompose them with an LLM into a natural instruction, and evaluate with an annotation-free three-dimension metric suite (NavInstrCritic).
insight: Explicit entity extraction beats both end-to-end trained generators and video-LLMs used directly: Qwen2.5-VL reaches MSC 2.872 versus NavComposer's 5.112. Ablations show each entity contributes: removing objects hurts matching and diversity most, and removing scenes collapses SSC (1.148). Module analysis shows action accuracy matters most (visual odometry 98.5% vs ResNet 67.3%), open-vocabulary multimodal LLMs beat closed-set detectors for objects, and a stronger LLM is not always a better synthesizer (GPT-4o-mini was worse than Qwen2.5-7B).
method: Action classification: predicts {stop, forward, left, right} from consecutive frames, using either SIFT+FLANN visual odometry with pose recovery or a ResNet50/DINOv2 encoder with an FC head fine-tuned on VLN-CE. Temporal correction fixes ABA patterns to AAA and AAB patterns by majority vote.
Scene recognition: per-frame scene phrase from a unimodal classifier (MAE on Places365, SWAG) or a prompted multimodal LLM (BLIP-2, LLaVA-1.6, Qwen2.5-VL, GPT-4o-mini).
Object detection: picks the most salient landmark with its egocentric position, either DETR/SWAG plus a nine-grid position rule or open-ended VQA with a multimodal LLM.

Instruction synthesis: takes action-based key-frame downsampling (start/middle/end of runs of identical actions, with random 'enter/pass/leave' for forward), double random synonym replacement (a per-instruction ratio M and a random synonym index) for diversity, then an LLM prompted with the ordered entity list writes the instruction.
NavInstrCritic contrastive matching: a CLIP-based trajectory-instruction matcher with video pooling, trained on VLN-CE, scored by HR, MRR, TIR and MAP in-batch retrieval.
NavInstrCritic semantic consistency: Qwen-14B rates how well the instruction reflects actions, scenes and objects (ASC, SSC, OSC, and their mean MSC, each 0-10).
NavInstrCritic linguistic diversity: MATTR, N-gram diversity, Self-BLEU and compression ratio.
End-to-end baseline: a CoCa model with video pooling fine-tuned on VLN-CE to generate instructions.

setting.backbone: Best variant vo-gpt-gpt-qwn: SIFT+FLANN visual odometry, GPT-4o-mini for scene and object, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct for synthesis (frozen). Offline variant vo-qwn-qwn-qwn uses Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen2.5-7B (frozen).
setting.training_data: Essentially none (training-free, dataset-agnostic) for the visual-odometry and LLM variants. Only optional action classifiers are fine-tuned on VLN-CE. The evaluation matcher is trained on the VLN-CE training set.
setting.action_space: Instruction generation only; inferred actions are stop / move forward / turn left / turn right
setting.simulator: VLN-CE trajectories (Habitat) plus HM3D, SceneNet, GRUtopia, and real datasets (SUN3D, ScanNet, TUM, 12-Scenes, DIODE, KITTI, NavTJ)

numbers_note: This paper evaluates instruction generation, not navigation success. Metrics are NavInstrCritic scores, and the split is a combination of VLN-CE seen and unseen, labeled 'val' here. Cross-dataset results (MAP/MSC/CR on 10 sources, e.g. HM3D MAP 0.62, KITTI MSC 5.49) are in Table diverse_generation and are not listed as entries.
results: NavComposer outperforms the fine-tuned end-to-end CoCa baseline (MSC 2.768), Speaker-Follower (2.258), EnvDrop (2.433) and video LLMs such as Qwen2.5-VL (MSC 2.872, MAP 0.675) on nearly all metrics, with MAP 0.685 and MSC 5.112. It generalizes to 10 diverse trajectory sources (232,569 instructions) without training. The offline 7B variant is only slightly worse (MSC 4.283).
limitations: Precise control of instruction style and granularity remains difficult.
The NavInstrCritic contrastive matcher is trained on VLN-CE, so it is biased and unreliable on other domains (low MAP on SceneNet, KITTI).
High computational cost for large-scale generation. Instruction quality is not validated by training navigation agents or by human evaluation.
